Xanax as needed in use by patient
Vitamin D in use by patient

Assessment.content: Right knee pain with activity-related clicking and intermittent effusion in a runner with increased training mileage over 2 weeks, likely due to overuse, soft-tissue, or cartilage-related etiology without red flags identified at present
Assessment.source_text: 1) Right knee pain with activity-related clicking and intermittent effusion, in a runner with increased training mileage over 2 weeks. Likely overuse/soft-tissue or cartilage-related etiology; no red flags identified at present.

Assessment.content: Post-exercise transient paresthesias in right toes
No current knee instability, locking, range of motion limitation, or acute infection signs
Assessment.source_text: 3) No current knee instability, locking, or ROM limitation; no acute infection signs.

Plan_of_Care.content: Continue ice therapy as much as possible and ice the knee after runs
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Ice therapy: continue as much as possible; ice after runs.

Plan_of_Care.content: Modify activity by easing running volume and intensity and avoid pain-provoking mileage while maintaining cross-training as tolerated
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Activity modification: ease running volume/intensity; avoid pain-provoking mileage; maintain cross-training as tolerated.

Plan_of_Care.content: Refer patient to physiotherapy for comprehensive knee assessment and rehabilitation program
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Physiotherapy: refer for comprehensive knee assessment and rehab program.

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider in-clinic evaluation if wait for physiotherapy is long
Plan_of_Care.source_text: If wait is long, consider in-clinic evaluation.

Plan_of_Care.content: Plan to obtain knee imaging to assess cartilage and structure if symptoms persist or if swelling, heat, or redness develops, or if the knee completely locks
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Imaging: plan to obtain knee imaging (cartilage/structural assessment) if symptoms persist or if swelling/heat/redness develops, or knee completely locks.

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe a stronger NSAID to replace ibuprofen, to be taken with food and not concurrently with ibuprofen
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Medications: prescribe a stronger anti-inflammatory (NSAID) to use regularly in place of ibuprofen, with instructions to take with food and not concurrently with ibuprofen.

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange follow-up after physiotherapy assessment or sooner if red flags develop
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Follow-up: arrange follow-up after physio assessment or sooner if red flags develop.

Plan_of_Care.content: Instruct patient to return urgently if knee swells with heat, redness, fever, or if knee completely locks or cannot be bent or straightened, or if patient feels unwell
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Urgent/警惕 signs: return urgently if knee swells with heat, redness, fever, or if knee completely locks or you cannot bend/straighten it, or you feel unwell.

Plan_of_Care.content: Counsel patient that ACL or ligament injury cannot be diagnosed reliably via videoconference, and that physiotherapy evaluation is the appropriate first step with imaging added if indicated
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Counseling: ACL/ligament injury cannot be diagnosed reliably via videoconference; physio evaluation is appropriate first step; imaging may be added if indicated.

Plan_of_Care.content: Send stronger NSAID prescription to patient’s pharmacy
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Pharmacy: send stronger NSAID prescription to your pharmacy.

Follow_up_Information.content: Follow-up is planned after physiotherapy assessment or sooner if red flag symptoms develop
Follow_up_Information.source_text: • Follow-up: arrange follow-up after physio assessment or sooner if red flags develop.

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient advised to return urgently if knee swells with heat, redness, fever, if knee completely locks or cannot be bent or straightened, or if patient feels unwell
